newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - April 11.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The prime minister has promised speedy resolution of the truck weight row and suggests semi-trailers will cause less damage to roads than 10-wheelers. The government will not try to put off the conflict but will make sure the issue is resolved quickly, says PM Chavalit Yongchaiyudh. (BANGKOK POST) (THE NATION)

- The signing of a contract to build a 3,300-million-baht nuclear research reactor in Thailand is being held up because the winning bidder has been unable to obtain safety approval for the design. Project leader the Office of Atomic Energy for Peace wants to get around the problem by requesting a change to the conditions so that the contract with General Atomic of the United States can be signed. (BANGKOK POST)

- Senators have put up tough resistance to the Constitution Drafting Assembly's (CDA) plan to propose the direct election of senators, which they warn will spread money politics and politicians' influence to the Upper House. The strong show of opposition is expressed at a CDA hearing by representatives of key wings of the Senate and provides a strong hint as to how the upper chamber will treat the constitutional draft if it is submitted to Parliament with a clause on senatorial elections. (THE NATION)

- The response by American investors to the government's US$500-million bond has been subdued because of the prevailing bearish sentiment in the U.S. fixed-income market. The deal, which is being promoted in a roadshow led by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan, was due to close yesterday. (THE NATION) (BUSINESS DAY)

- Powerful equipment suppliers and their local partners have colluded prior to submitting bids for a combined 17 billion baht worth of contracts for the Telephone Organisation of Thailand. The agreement is expected to hasten the bid evaluation process after months of delay due to power plays among the giant firms. (THE NATION)
